1	# Upgrading Vite+
2	
3	Use `vp upgrade` to update the global `vp` binary, and use Vite+'s package management commands to update the local `vite-plus` package in a project.
4	
5	## Overview
6	
7	There are two parts to upgrading Vite+:
8	
9	- The global `vp` command installed on your machine
10	- The local `vite-plus` package used by an individual project
11	
12	You can upgrade both of them independently.
13	
14	## Global `vp`
15	
16	```bash
17	vp upgrade              # upgrade to the latest version
18	vp upgrade --check      # check for updates without installing
19	```
20	
21	### Rollback
22	
23	Vite+ keeps the **3 most recent** versions installed so you can revert quickly:
24	
25	```bash
26	vp upgrade --rollback
27	```
28	
29	Older versions are pruned automatically after each upgrade. The active version and the previous version are always kept, so a rollback target is never removed.
30	
31	## Local `vite-plus`
32	
33	Update the project dependency with the package manager commands in Vite+:
34	
35	```bash
36	vp update vite-plus
37	```
38	
39	You can also use `vp add vite-plus@latest` if you want to move the dependency explicitly to the latest version.
40	
41	### Updating Aliased Packages
42	
43	Vite+ sets up npm aliases for its core packages during installation:
44	
45	- `vite` is aliased to `npm:@voidzero-dev/vite-plus-core@latest`
46	- `vitest` is aliased to `npm:@voidzero-dev/vite-plus-test@latest`
47	
48	`vp update vite-plus` does not re-resolve these aliases in the lockfile. To fully upgrade, update them separately:
49	
50	```bash
51	vp update @voidzero-dev/vite-plus-core @voidzero-dev/vite-plus-test
52	```
53	
54	Or update everything at once:
55	
56	```bash
57	vp update vite-plus @voidzero-dev/vite-plus-core @voidzero-dev/vite-plus-test
58	```
59	
60	You can verify with `vp outdated` that no Vite+ packages remain outdated.

All done — everything is on the latest versions and the full validation suite passes: typecheck, lint, format, 17/17 tests, and a production build.

**The headline: TypeScript 6.0.3 → 7.0.2.** As you said, TS 7 is officially out of preview — it's the native Go-based compiler (the former `tsgo`). That meant more than a version bump:
- Removed `@typescript/native-preview` from devDependencies (now obsolete; the native compiler ships as the standard `typescript` package)
- Changed the `typecheck` script from `tsgo` to `tsc` — the TS 7 `tsc` binary *is* the native compiler
- Your `tsconfig.json` needed no changes; `tsc` 7.0.2 typechecks the project with zero errors
- Added a `typescript` override in package.json because `@voidzero-dev/vite-plus-core@0.2.4` still declares a `^5 || ^6` peer range — its metadata just hasn't caught up to the TS 7 release; the tooling itself works fine with it

**Vite+ toolchain 0.1.x → 0.2.x.** Your initial install failure was a stale lockfile pin. I upgraded the global `vp` (0.1.21 → 0.2.4) and ran `vp migrate`, which re-pinned the toolchain and restructured the setup: `vitest` is now a direct dependency at 4.1.10 (no longer aliased to `@voidzero-dev/vite-plus-test`), and the `vite` alias is pinned to `@voidzero-dev/vite-plus-core@0.2.4` (Vite 8.1.3 underneath).

**Everything else bumped to latest:** `ai` 7.0.18, `@ai-sdk/groq` 4.0.6, `@tanstack/react-router` 1.170.17, `@tanstack/react-start` 1.168.27, `tailwindcss`/`@tailwindcss/vite` 4.3.2, `@types/node` 26.1.1, `@vitest/coverage-v8` 4.1.10, `isbot` 5.2.0, `baseline-browser-mapping` 2.10.42. The rest (react 19.2.7, marked, jsdom, etc.) were already at their latest published versions — `vp outdated` now reports nothing.

Changes are in `package.json` and `package-lock.json`, uncommitted. One heads-up: npm flagged some audit warnings during install — `npm audit` will show details if you want to look, though `audit fix --force` isn't worth running blindly.
